say: Each format has three checks. A voice note puts the main point in the first ten seconds, has no noise covering words, and types the key number underneath. A photo is sharp and shows the key detail. A video is under two minutes, steady and audible.

panel.heading: Three checks, scored 0 to 2
items: Voice note: point in the first ten seconds
Photo: sharp, bright, key detail visible
Video: under two minutes, every step audible
Score 0, 1 or 2 per check: out of 6
Ask a question someone can really answer

say: Score each check 0, 1 or 2, for a score out of 6. Do not aim for 6 on day one. Aim to raise your usual score by one point over a few weeks.

say: When you ask for feedback, do not ask: was it OK? Ask: did you understand the new date the first time, or did you have to replay it?

panel.rule: Change only one thing at a time, and write it down.

say: Professionals use a rule called 3-2-1: three copies, on two kinds of storage, with one copy somewhere else. The first copy is the original on your phone.

cards.d: The copy you carry every day. It can be lost, stolen or dropped in water.
Google Photos or Google Drive. Turn backup on, on Wi-Fi only if data is costly.
For the most precious files: a computer or memory card at home or with a trusted relative.

say: The second is in the cloud. In Google Photos, tap your profile picture, open Photos settings, find Backup and turn it on. A free Google account includes 15 GB, shared with Gmail and Drive.

cards.d: The copy you carry every day. It can be lost, stolen or dropped in water.
Google Photos or Google Drive. Turn backup on, on Wi-Fi only if data is costly.
For the most precious files: a computer or memory card at home or with a trusted relative.

say: The third, for the most precious files, is a computer or memory card kept at home or with a trusted relative.

say: For example, Esther in Jos has a free Google account, and Gmail and Drive already use 2 GB. That leaves 13 GB, about 13,000 MB.

panel.heading: Esther checks before she backs up
items: Space left: 15 GB minus 2 GB = 13 GB
Photos: 3,000 x 3 MB = 9,000 MB
Videos: about 6,000 MB. Total 15,000 MB
Too much: delete duplicates, then back up

say: Her 3,000 photos average about 3 MB each, which is 9,000 MB. Her videos come to about 6,000 MB. Together that is 15,000 MB, more than she has.

panel.heading: Esther checks before she backs up
items: Space left: 15 GB minus 2 GB = 13 GB
Photos: 3,000 x 3 MB = 9,000 MB
Videos: about 6,000 MB. Total 15,000 MB
Too much: delete duplicates, then back up

say: So she deletes about 500 duplicate and blurry photos and 15 forwarded videos, then backs up the rest on Wi-Fi. Simple subtraction first saves a backup that stops halfway.

say: Your WhatsApp chats need their own backup: Settings, Chats, Chat backup. Anyone who gets into your account can see your photos, so use a strong password, turn on two-step verification, and never share its codes.
If your phone is lost, report the line so your SIM can be blocked.

panel.heading: WhatsApp and account safety

Two-step verification turned on
Never share the codes it sends you

say: To remember. Score your messages, count real signals, and change one thing at a time. Keep three copies of what matters. And before you submit, check that no account numbers or PINs appear.
